investigations.kind: Frame-level video analysis · three cameras, one camera original · V2
investigations.title: Two gestures before the shot
investigations.question: Did two men on the security line press something in the seconds before the shot, and try to hide it?
investigations.finding: Zero is the frame in which Kirk's head snaps back (2.MOV 520, 16.mp4 193, 7.mp4 770), tied across the clips by their shared sound to about 0.1 s. The plaid-shirt man's right hand leaves the barrier rail 0.50 s before that frame and his index finger is on his left sleeve 0.40 s before it; no button, strap or device resolves at 1080p. The blue-shirt man's arms stay folded through it with the right hand hidden; Kirk's own arm covers the fold for the last 0.16 s and the right fist emerges 0.10 s after. The white-polo man first taken for the sleeve-scratcher is holding a phone.
investigations.limitations: A hand out of view cannot be shown still. The anchor is a human reading of one frame per clip, checked by audio alignment to about 0.1 s and by a second person's movement. The plaid-shirt man is seen from one camera. No blinded rating was run; purpose is not addressed.

levels.observable_movement: yes, catalogued per frame for every hand in view
levels.identifiable_action: white-polo man: a phone; plaid-shirt man: none resolved (a finger on cloth); blue-shirt man: hand occluded, not observable

versions.label: V1
versions.note: Anchored on the loudest audio transient per file; in 2.MOV that was a crowd burst 2.25 s before the shot, which reversed the plaid-shirt finding. Withdrawn the same day; kept in git history.

versions.label: V2
versions.note: Anchored on Kirk's first visible movement per clip, cross-checked by audio cross-correlation between clips and by the blue-shirt man's movement in the 2.MOV foreground. Close-up loops added.

investigations.kind: Independent review by ChatGPT Astra · four sources · reproduced with an editor's note
investigations.title: Movement and timing: a second review
investigations.question: What does ChatGPT Astra's separate review of the same files conclude, and where does it differ?
investigations.finding: Same frames, same observations. The review confirms sleeve contact at frames 487–492 of 2.MOV before Kirk's visible reaction and unfolding at 199–202 of 16.mp4 after it, resolves no control or object, and finds the folded posture 21 s earlier. Its zero in each file is about 0.3 s before the head snap study 01 V2 uses; the order it reports is unaffected. Study 01 V1 disputed its zero and was wrong.
investigations.limitations: Frame brackets chosen by the reviewing model, no audio reference, no blinded rating. Reproduced in the review's own words; the editor's note was rewritten with study 01 V2 and the earlier note withdrawn.
